purpose: Exact, unsummarized staging store for v7 source content (Board bullets, Clinical Impact statements, and exact drug-specific clinical flags) that cannot fit the current canonical flat schema without schema expansion.
policy: Fidelity audit correction: zero placeholders, zero generic flag copy-pasting, exact source text preservation.

unmapped_board_high_yield_en: Vitamin K antagonist requiring strict INR monitoring.
Major/fatal bleeding is the central toxicity.
Diet, drugs, and supplements can alter anticoagulant effect.
Classic comparison: Warfarin (vitamin K pathway + INR monitoring) vs DOAC Xa inhibitors (-xaban; no routine INR titration) vs antiplatelets (clopidogrel on platelets).

clinical_impact_en: Bleeding or bruising reported by the patient may be medication related.
Changes in diet, supplements, or new medications can alter anticoagulant effect.
Patients taking warfarin require monitoring of INR values.
Acupuncture relevance: Do not interpret bruising or bleeding tendency without considering anticoagulant therapy; present a bleeding-risk prompt.

unmapped_board_high_yield_en: -xaban -> factor Xa inhibitor.
Do not abruptly discontinue without appropriate anticoagulation planning: current label warns of increased thrombotic risk.
Neuraxial/spinal procedures carry spinal/epidural hematoma risk.

clinical_impact_en: Stopping anticoagulation prematurely can expose the patient to thrombotic risk.
Any planned neuraxial procedure has a specific label warning.

unmapped_board_high_yield_en: P2Y12 platelet inhibitor antiplatelet (P in clopidogrel/aspirin -> platelets).
Requires metabolic activation through CYP2C19; boxed warning on reduced effect in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers.
Bleeding remains a major clinical safety concern.

clinical_impact_en: Genetics/drug interactions affecting CYP2C19 may reduce efficacy.

unmapped_board_high_yield_en: Dual lens: NSAID (prostaglandin/COX pathway, pain/inflammation) and low-dose antiplatelet.
Course emphasizes gastric irritation/erosion, hemorrhage, renal injury, and Reye syndrome risk in children with viral illness.
Compare with acetaminophen: analgesic/antipyretic but not a classic anti-inflammatory NSAID.

clinical_impact_en: High-value card because patients commonly combine aspirin with fish oil, supplements, or herbs.
Each interaction must be graded by evidence; blood-moving alone is not proof of a clinically significant interaction.

unmapped_board_high_yield_en: Injectable Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin (LMWH); distinguish from oral warfarin and DOACs.
Appears in perioperative, thromboembolism, pregnancy/fertility or recurrent-loss medical contexts.

clinical_impact_en: Medication should trigger a bleeding/bruising review and awareness of injection-site bruising.

unmapped_board_high_yield_en: -SARTAN -> ARB. Blocks angiotensin II receptor signaling.
Hypertension, diabetic nephropathy context, hyperkalemia, renal function, hypotension.
Boxed warning for fetal toxicity.
Compare ACE inhibitor -pril: ARB avoids ACE inhibition cough but shares RAS-related potassium, renal and pregnancy issues.

clinical_impact_en: Dizziness, low BP (especially with volume depletion), renal function deterioration, and elevated potassium.
Acupuncture relevance: Surface BP/volume/electrolyte context before symptoms like dizziness or weakness are assigned entirely to a TCM deficiency pattern.

unmapped_board_high_yield_en: Thiazide diuretic.
Course mnemonic: See No Evil and high-yield association with secondary angle-closure glaucoma.
Classic electrolyte associations: hypokalemia, hyponatremia and volume changes.
Compare: furosemide (loop, stronger diuresis, ototoxicity) vs spironolactone (potassium-sparing, hyperkalemia) vs HCTZ (thiazide, hypokalemia/hyponatremia).

clinical_impact_en: Cramps / weakness, dizziness / hypotension, confusion in electrolyte disturbance, acute eye pain / visual change in secondary angle-closure glaucoma.
Acupuncture relevance: Leg cramps, fatigue, weakness and dizziness can be over-attributed to Qi/Blood deficiency if medication/electrolyte effects are not visible.
